bull.b: Rapid DTC growth strengthens control over pricing, customer relationships, and product presentation while improving channel mix. A rising share of company-owned sales can support brand consistency and profitability over the next several quarters, provided demand remains broad-based.

High and improving gross and EBITDA margins indicate meaningful brand pricing power and operating leverage as revenue scales. Management’s reiterated margin targets suggest profitability is being treated as a core operating outcome, supporting stronger reinvestment and cash generation.

A growing net cash position gives On financial flexibility to fund product innovation, retail expansion, and new sports categories without relying heavily on additional borrowing. Strong liquidity also improves resilience if channel conditions or consumer demand become less favorable.

bear.b: Deliberately reducing wholesale sell-in protects full-price positioning but creates a near-term constraint on reported revenue and channel scale. The lower cadence may persist until new product launches and improved retail sell-through restore stronger wholesale momentum.

A sizeable inventory increase raises the importance of disciplined purchasing and sell-through across channels. If demand or wholesale activity does not absorb the added units, On could face greater working-capital needs or pressure to use promotions, potentially weighing on margins.

Higher import tariffs can pressure product economics and cash flow, particularly in the U.S. market, until refunds or other offsets are realized. Because the timing of those benefits remains uncertain, near-term margins and earnings conversion may be less predictable.
